skills.name: Upjohn
skills.description: Properly identifies representation and role with the Company, and that they cannot give the employee legal advice. This must always be part of the very beginning of the interview.
skills.reason: The interviewer gave a full Upjohn warning at the very start (T2), covering the Committee and company as client, no personal representation, no legal advice, and an invitation to ask questions.

skills.name: Privilege
skills.description: Properly explains that the Company controls the privilege and determines how it is shared.
skills.reason: T2 explains that the privilege belongs to the company, that the company decides whether to waive it, and that it may disclose what is learned without the witness's consent. T4 then checked the witness's understanding.

skills.name: Relationship
skills.description: Establishes rapport and interview expectations. This includes: establishes an appropriate professional tone; explains how the interview will proceed; encourages complete answers; instructs the witness that they can speculate, they just need to say when they do; invites the witness to distinguish between recollection and uncertainty.
skills.reason: T6 sets out how the interview will proceed, asks for complete answers, tells the witness to flag speculation and to say whether a memory is recalled or reconstructed, and invites clarification requests.

skills.name: Confirmation
skills.description: Checks the witness understood the Upjohn warning and answers their questions, if any.
skills.reason: T4 asked the witness to restate who was represented and who controlled privilege, and T6 confirmed that the witness could consult their own lawyer. The witness's stated concern about counsel was answered.

skills.name: Closing
skills.description: Closes by confirming there is "nothing else", next steps, a confidentiality reminder, and a reminder to keep records.
skills.reason: T356 covers confidentiality, record retention, not discussing with other witnesses and a possible follow-up, and asks whether there is anything to add. It does not expressly confirm there is nothing else in those words.

moments.text: To be clear, we represent the Committee and the company only. We do not represent you personally, we are not your attorney, and we can't give you legal advice.
Explained that the privilege belongs to the company, that the company decides whether to waive it, and that it may disclose what is learned without the witness's consent.
Asked the witness to restate in their own words who was represented and who controlled the privilege, and the witness answered correctly at T5.
Please give me complete answers, even if a detail seems minor.
Set out the interview structure and ground rules, including flagging speculation and distinguishing recollection from reconstruction.
Please keep all related documents and notes, keep today confidential, and don't discuss it with other witnesses.
The witness said they had nothing to add after the interviewer asked whether there was anything to add or correct.

skills.name: Narrative Development
skills.description: Lets the witness walk through what happened.
skills.reason: Open invitations such as 'Tell me everything you remember' (T16, T32, T44, T80) let the witness walk through LJM1, the Rhythms unwind, and Chewco in their own words before specific questions.

skills.name: Funneling
skills.description: Moves in a sensible order from general to specific questions.
skills.reason: The interview moves from role and reporting lines (T8-T15) to open narratives and then to specific documents and figures. Some topic jumps, such as moving from Chewco to LJM2 controls at T80, are less tightly sequenced.

skills.name: Clarity
skills.description: Asks clear questions and avoids compound, ambiguous, or legalistic questions.
skills.reason: Most questions are short and clear, for example T8, T34-T37 and T144. A few are awkward or compound, such as T304 'Who would the Andy it's addressed to be?'

skills.name: Professionalism
skills.description: Stays neutral, polite and in control.
skills.reason: The tone stays neutral and polite throughout, even when the witness is evasive. Questions such as T306 'Help me understand how those fit together' keep control without accusation.

skills.name: Adaptability
skills.description: Changes technique based on the witness's answers rather than staying only with the outline.
skills.reason: The interviewer changed approach as answers developed: pressing for an estimate after a non-answer (T114-T119), pinning down the Foundation's return (T142-T151), and pursuing the Chewco note and the payment after counsel's advice (T300-T333).

moments.text: Tell me everything you remember about how LJM1 came about in 1999.
Tell me everything you remember about how Chewco came to be formed in 1997.
Approximately, then. Were they above or below the 30 percent the Board was shown?
What's your best estimate?
Help me understand how those fit together.
A somewhat awkwardly phrased question about who the Andy in the note was.

areas.name: Fact Development, Source Identification, & Credibility Testing

skills.name: Ensures Credibility
skills.description: Recognizes and follows up on incomplete, evasive, or inconsistent answers.
skills.reason: Evasive or inconsistent answers were consistently followed up, including the Chewco 'Skilling told the Board' answer (T55-T57), the Foundation and Southampton answers (T122-T169) and the Chewco note contradiction (T306-T309).

skills.name: Material Facts
skills.description: Identifies the who, what, when, and how.
skills.reason: The interviewer systematically covered who, what, when and how for Southampton, the Raptor approvals (T104-T109), the Chewco buyout figure (T274-T299) and the $2.6M payment (T310-T333).

skills.name: Memory Refreshing
skills.description: Tries other ways when the witness can't remember.
skills.reason: T62 asked whether notes or minutes could help the witness remember, and T70-T75 showed the minutes to test recall. T144-T147 asked which records would show the exact amount.

skills.name: Establishes Knowledge
skills.description: Separates what the witness personally knows from speculation, secondhand information, or inferences.
skills.reason: The interviewer asked how the witness knew things (T56, T82, T226, T235-T237, T346), separating personal knowledge from what was reported or assumed.

skills.name: Other Sources
skills.description: Identifies additional witnesses.
skills.reason: T336-T342 identified Causey, Buy, Glisan, Kopper, McMahon, Skilling and Lay as further sources, and T40-T43 pursued who in Causey's group reviewed the unwind.

skills.name: Other Evidence
skills.description: Identifies other documents such as communications, reports, notes, or other relevant records.
skills.reason: The interviewer asked about minutes, the Foundation's account statements (T350), and personal notes and emails (T352-T355), and identified deal files, approval sheets and partnership agreements (T348-T349).

skills.name: Tests Certainty
skills.description: Examines how certain the witness is about their memory or a fact.
skills.reason: The interviewer asked how sure the witness was about key figures, for example T144-T145 on the $4.5M, T216-T217 on the three hours and T222-T223 on the $229M, and T318-T319 on timing.

skills.name: Follow-Up
skills.description: Recognizes material responses and follows up on them.
skills.reason: Material answers were followed up in depth, such as the Foundation's $4.5M return (T142-T151), the Chewco figure rising to $10M (T280-T299), and the counsel call before the payment (T314-T333).

I don't know that personally. That was my understanding.

How do you know that: did you see it yourself, or did someone tell you?
Asked whether the witness could produce the Foundation's account statements for 2000.
Asked whether the witness had personal files, notes or emails about LJM, Chewco or Southampton.

skills.name: Effective Selection
skills.description: Selects and contextualizes documents effectively, and properly authenticates the document.
skills.reason: Documents were introduced after recall questions and with context: the minutes (T62-T70), the Southampton agreement (T126-T135), the investor report (T194-T200) and the Chewco note (T300). Authenticity was addressed through signature, preparer and completeness questions (T72, T132-T135, T198).

skills.name: Narrative
skills.description: Gets the witness's story first, before using conflicting evidence.
skills.reason: The witness's account was taken first in each case, for example Raptor I's utilization (T246-T251) before the minutes quote (T252), and Chewco's structure (T44-T65) before the minutes (T70).

skills.name: Accuracy
skills.description: Describes the document accurately.
skills.reason: Document descriptions match the case record, such as the $25,000 and $4.5M Southampton figures (T136, T142), the $10.5M note (T300) and the April 2001 'not at risk' language quoted verbatim (T260).

skills.name: Avoid Initial Conclusion
skills.description: Separates the document from inferences or conclusions, unless the witness takes an unreasonable stance.
skills.reason: Mostly neutral, but T210 asks whether the Board should have known returns were several times what it had been told, and T332 summarizes the witness's account in a way that frames it before the witness answers.

skills.name: Fairness
skills.description: Provides the witness with a fair opportunity to explain any inconsistencies or disagreements with the document.
skills.reason: The witness was given room to reconcile differences, for example on the minutes (T252-T253), the Chewco note (T306-T307), the 'not at risk' language (T260-T265) and the Foundation investment (T150-T151).

moments.text: I'd like to show you the minutes of the November 5, 1997 Executive Committee meeting. Do you recognize them?
Asked who prepared the minutes, establishing their source.
Asked what the witness remembered about Southampton Place before showing the partnership agreement.
I'm now going to show you a document: a partnership agreement for Southampton Place, dated March 20, 2000. Do you recognize it?

Is this a complete copy of what was sent to the investors?
The minutes record you saying there had been tremendous utilization of Raptor I.
Quoted the April 2001 investor update's 'was not at risk' language accurately and asked whether the witness had said that.
I'm not suggesting you wrote it. Do you recognize it?
Help me understand how those fit together.

missed_opportunities: T39: The witness said 'I don't recall anyone objecting' to the unwind. The interviewer did not follow up on whether anyone, such as Kaminski or Buy's group, had raised concerns about the Raptor or Rhythms transactions, which the case documents indicate.

T177: The witness said Anne Yaeger 'helped with LJM's administration' and was invited into Southampton. The interviewer did not ask about her marriage to Trushar Patel, who was responsible for later Raptors, which the case documents flag as a conflict.
tips: When a witness says 'I don't recall anyone objecting' or 'I don't recall concerns being raised,' ask: 'Who in Finance, Treasury or Accounting was closest to this deal, and did any of them ever voice a concern to you or to anyone you know of?'

When a witness describes a family member or colleague as someone who helped with a transaction, ask: 'What is this person's relationship to other people involved in the deals, and did they have any financial stake in the same transactions?'
